description:
## Goal

Produce reference-validated FER-vs-SNR curves for the DVB-T2
BCH(outer) + LDPC(inner) + BICM chain over an AWGN channel for three
canonical operating points: Normal frame (N=64800), code rates 1/2,
2/3, 3/4, modulations 16-QAM and 64-QAM Gray-mapped. Six (rate ×
modulation) curves total.

Before any campaign-grade simulation is run, the shared simulation
harness (`crates/gf2-coding/src/simulation.rs`) must be made observable
and resumable so that multi-hour runs survive crashes and can be tailed
live without modifying the binary.

## Context

DVB-T2 BCH outer (`crates/gf2-coding/src/bch/dvb_t2/`) covers all 12
ETSI configurations and is verified by unit tests. DVB-T2 LDPC inner
(`crates/gf2-coding/src/ldpc/dvb_t2/`) has all 12 parity-check tables
populated as Rust constants and the TP04 → TP05 → TP06 portion of the
ETSI test-vector chain (VV001-CR35, 202/202 blocks) is verified end to
end.

What is missing for closure of the AWGN slice of milestone f0448e55:

1. The column-row bit interleaver from EN 302 755 §6.1.3 (only a
   random-seed-based interleaver exists today in
   `crates/gf2-coding/src/fading.rs`).
2. Concatenation glue that drives BCH then LDPC then BICM in one path.
3. Validation up to TP07a (post-interleaver).
4. A campaign runner binary that produces the actual curves and plots.
5. Logging / progress / checkpoint-resume infrastructure in
   `SimulationRunner` so 10⁶-frame runs are safe to launch unattended.
6. The 11 missing LDPC parity-table source files in `.txt` form (Rust
   constants are present but not the ETSI tables they derive from),
   for auditability.

This epic delivers items 1-6 in dependency order. The integration
milestone (f0448e55) closes when this epic plus the GNU Radio OOT
story (b8baca8a) are both done. The SDR hardware demo (fcb09e6f) is
explicitly out of scope.

## Configurations covered

| Frame  | Code rate | N (LDPC) | k (LDPC) | k_bch  | Modulations    |
|--------|-----------|----------|----------|--------|----------------|
| Normal | 1/2       | 64 800   | 32 400   | 32 208 | 16-QAM, 64-QAM |
| Normal | 2/3       | 64 800   | 43 200   | 43 040 | 16-QAM, 64-QAM |
| Normal | 3/4       | 64 800   | 48 600   | 48 408 | 16-QAM, 64-QAM |

## Reference for validation

ETSI TS 102 831 v1.2.1 (2012-08), "Implementation guidelines for a
second generation digital terrestrial television broadcasting system
(DVB-T2)". The implementation-guidelines document contains AWGN
simulation curves for each MODCOD; those are the comparison baseline.
The hand-extracted reference points are checked in by task NEW-2
under `crates/gf2-coding/data/dvb_t2_tr102831_reference.toml`.

## Success criteria

- [hard] For each of the 6 (rate × modulation) curves, the simulated
  FER matches the ETSI TS 102 831 reference at FER = 10⁻⁴ within
  **0.5 dB** of Es/N₀ for the three 16-QAM curves and **0.65 dB** for
  the three 64-QAM curves.
  AMENDMENT 2026-06-13 (user-approved via project-lead escalation;
  see child e4849f07 for the full record): the ETSI TS 102 831
  Table 44 anchors assume "Genie-Aided" demapping, which the spec
  (§14.2, above Table 44) states is "optimistic ... for high-order
  constellations." The in-scope single-pass ExactLogMap BICM is
  below the genie bound, so the gap grows with constellation order.
  Observed gaps: 16-QAM {1/2: 0.167, 2/3: 0.117, 3/4: 0.224} dB;
  64-QAM {1/2: 0.606, 2/3: 0.585, 3/4: 0.514} dB. All six curves
  meet the amended criterion.
- [aspirational] Tighter gap of **0.3 dB** at FER = 10⁻⁴ on each curve,
  recorded per curve in the closure note where met.
- [hard] The full TP04 → TP05 → TP06 → TP07a ETSI test-vector chain is
  bit-exact (satisfied transitively via 4cdaf1c5).
- [hard] The deepest plotted SNR point on each curve has ≥ 10⁶
  simulated frames, and the SNR point bracketing FER = 10⁻⁴ from
  above (FER ≥ 10⁻⁴) has ≥ 100 frame errors.
  AMENDMENT 2026-06-13 (user-approved via project-lead escalation;
  see child e4849f07 for the full record): the original wording
  ("at every measured SNR point bracketing FER = 10⁻⁴, ≥ 100 frame
  errors") is replaced by its own operative parenthetical
  ("≥ 10⁶ frames at the deepest SNR plotted"). The N=64800
  waterfall is a near-vertical cliff (~1 decade per 0.045 dB), so
  the measured point just below 10⁻⁴ sits at FER ~ 10⁻⁵ where
  ≥ 100 errors would need 5–24 × 10⁶ frames/curve. The data meets
  the amended bar: 1.2 × 10⁶ frames at every deepest plotted point
  and ≥ 100 errors at each above-cliff bracketing point.
- [hard] Campaign artefacts are checked in under
  `dev/benchmarks/dvb_t2_awgn/`:
  - one CSV per (rate × modulation) curve,
  - one PNG overlay per (rate × modulation) showing simulated vs
    ETSI TS 102 831 reference (produced by the operator-run plotting
    script in `dev/benchmarks/dvb_t2_awgn/`, not the binary itself),
  - one JSON tracing log per campaign run,
  - `README.md` recording invocation, RNG seed, host info, wall-clock.
- [hard] A campaign run interrupted by SIGINT or process kill after at
  least one SNR point has completed resumes from the next unfinished
  SNR point on restart, without recomputing finished work. Validated
  by an integration test that kills the runner mid-campaign and
  verifies the resumed CSV is bit-identical to an uninterrupted
  reference run with the same seed.
- [hard] All campaign progress is emitted as structured `tracing`
  events to a JSON file (one record per SNR point completion plus
  configurable per-N-frames heartbeats), tailable with `jq` during the
  run. No live TUI or progress bar.
- [hard] A CLI binary reproduces every published curve via a single
  invocation per config.

## Out of scope (explicit)

- SDR / hardware reception (fcb09e6f).
- GNU Radio OOT decoder blocks (b8baca8a).
- Fading channels (TU6 / Rayleigh / Rician).
- Time interleaver, frequency interleaver, frame builder above the
  bit-interleaver layer.
- LDPC decoder algorithm changes — use the existing belief-propagation
  decoder. Tuning parameters (max iterations, schedule) allowed if
  needed to hit the gap target.
title: DVB-T2 AWGN simulation campaign — Normal frame, rates 1/2 / 2/3 / 3/4
